title: Sequence stamp desync after gateway reshard corrupts nested function output
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer reported that nested function/tool outputs are occasionally being merged or misattributed when requests traverse gateway reshard events. The problem appears after gateway reshards and retries: streaming segments that belong to one invocation are re-emitted with stale sequence stamps and get coalesced into another in-flight invocation, corrupting structured output (JSON envelopes and function return blobs). This has been observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, with the most reproducible cases on Dedicated when a gateway reshard and client retry overlap with a partial KV-cache eviction.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use high-throughput client to invoke function-calling model with nested tool calls (two-stage: model -> toolA -> toolB).
2) Trigger gateway reshard by scaling up the gateway pool during the run (or simulate using test harness to force shard reassignment).
3) Induce a retry path (network transient) so some stream segments are retransmitted from the previous shard while a new invocation continues on the new shard.
4) Observe merged/misattributed tool outputs in the final structured JSON (see examples in investigation notes).
investigation_notes: 2026-02-16: Customer (ACME Inc, case CS-4479) reported ~2% of production calls returned tool outputs that belonged to a prior invocation. Provided request/response capture and trace IDs.

2026-02-18: Reproduced on dedicated-us-west2 using load test harness. Found two triggering conditions: gateway reshard + partial retransmit from previous connection; and concurrent KV-cache eviction that dropped prefix anchors used by the parser.

Root cause hypothesis: Gateway reshard logic assigns per-stream sequence stamps non-monotonically when a shard hands off active connections. Retransmitted segments retain old stream stamps but are accepted by the new shard because the per-invocation flow identifier is not strictly validated across shard handoff. Parser merges segments based on stamp ordering, resulting in envelope interleaving.
Edge condition: When nested function outputs include identical envelope markers (rare but possible for some tool outputs), the parser's simple last-write merging becomes destructive rather than safe.
Telemetry: Grafana shows a spike of "stream-seq-rewrite" events coincident with gateway reshard windows. See dashboard link.
temporary_mitigation: 2026-02-20: Deployed hotfix on dedicated-us-west2 that pins open connections to their original gateway shard for 30s after a reshard event. Reduced customer error rate from 2% -> 0.1% for ACME traffic.
Added conservative server-side validation: reject retransmitted segments where flow-id mismatch occurs (fails fast and triggers retry rather than silent merge).
Customer workaround: recommend client-side idempotency token and short exponential backoff to reduce in-flight overlap during gateway scaling windows.
proposed_fix: 1) Make sequence stamp allocation monotonic and globally unique per flow: add a 64-bit monotonic seq + 32-bit shard-epoch so stamps are comparable across shards.
2) Require a strong flow identifier (flow-id + instance-id) with every streaming segment and make shard handoff atomically transfer active flow ownership.
3) Parser hardening: treat out-of-order/stale segments as separate envelopes instead of merging; add explicit idempotency markers for nested tool outputs.
4) Add unit/e2e tests that simulate reshard + retransmit + KV eviction to prevent regressions.
Implementation owner: Marco Chen (runtime/streaming team). Code changes will touch gateway reshard logic, stream envelope validation, and parser.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): pin connections during reshard windows (deployed 2026-02-20) for highest-severity customers; monitor for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (core fix): land monotonic stamps + flow transfer (runtime-2.4.1); roll out to Dedicated then Hosted, with canary on Private customers who opt-in.
Phase 3 (parser hardening): deploy parser changes in runtime-2.5.0 and enable strict validation by default; provide opt-out flag for legacy clients for 30 days.
Backports: patch runtime-2.3.x for long-lived Dedicated contracts if requested by customers (evaluate per-customer SLA).
